speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, could you please tell me your age and when you first noticed the tremors and memory issues?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old man accompanied by his wife. The patient first noticed the tremor in his left hand 1 year ago, which has been progressively worsening. Recently, he has faced difficulty in performing tasks that require steadiness, such as reading. His wife has observed a decline in his memory, taking note of his forgetfulness in paying bills, a task she has since had to assume.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you. Do you experience the tremor when your hand is at rest, or does it mainly occur when you are trying to use your hand for tasks? Also, have you noticed any stiffness in your limbs or a slowing down of your movements?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Resting tremor worse on the left hand. I also have Soft speech, Reduced facial expressions, Memory decline, Difficulty in managing finances.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. Do you also experience any non-motor symptoms, such as changes in sleep patterns, constipation, or a loss of smell? Additionally, have you noticed any imbalance or frequent falls when walking?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Hypertension, medicated with aspirin and amlodipine. Family history of schizophrenia in his mother. No other significant medical or psychiatric history. Social history: Drinks 1-2 beers nightly and is a former cigar smoker.

speaker: Doctor
text: I have noted your history of hypertension and family history of schizophrenia. To help distinguish between different types of parkinsonism, do you experience visual hallucinations, or have you noticed that your symptoms do not improve significantly with standard Parkinson's medication?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies any other systemic complaints. Specifically, no urinary symptoms, no significant changes in bowel habits, no reported falls or dizziness.
